column1: # Game profile of 13 Sentinels: Aegis Rim (Switch, base game v0 + update 1.10 = v65536). In bring-up: on the Mac a new game gets through the prologue into the first battle
# Vanillaware's own engine, SDK 11.4.3 (sdk and subsdk0 are byte-identical to Metroid Dread's), NVN; all data is in 6 CRI CPK archives (ROBO_*.CPK), audio is CRI ADX2 (acb / awb), movies are CRI USM.
# The shaders are not in RomFS: 838 GLSLC compiler outputs (magic 0x19866891) are compiled into main's read-only segment and referenced from a table in .data (read by shader_split.py glslc_shaders)

# Game name: only a label for profile listings and the Mac window title; the iOS app name is the game name in the base NSP, and the bundle ID comes from the base game title ID (build_ipa.sh / NSP script)
# only the merged 1.10 copy is extracted; the base game's own build IDs are added when needed
# load order as on Horizon: main, subsdk*, sdk (subsdk0 = NintendoSDK_movie 11.4.3)

# The NPDM declares no system resource (META +0x14 = 0): the game uses SetHeapSize. main's bss is only about 21 MB. Measured (DM_SVC=1): the heap request is pool − used = 0xc9400000 (3.14 GB); the alias region gets one page during SDK initialization;

# thread stacks go into the stack region through MapMemory. Block = 256 MB in front + 256 MB alias region + 256 MB stack region + 3.25 GB heap region = 4 GB. On the Mac about 2.2 GB is resident in the first battle

# The engine cuts ring heaps out of a memory pool at 64 KB GPU alignment, and the pool's storage comes from malloc: allocations of 64 KB or more are 64 KB aligned (hle_os.c), or the third ring heap keeps base 0
# ---- Shader split (shader_split.py: GLSLC outputs in main, each a single-stage program, 838 ProgramSetShaders at startup; BindProgram's stage bits combine vertex and pixel per draw) ----
# the NVN depth mode the game sets (nvnDeviceSetDepthMode near = 0): the pipeline archive made offline holds the main0_z vertex entries (dm/gfx/tools/pso_offline.py)
